item.title: Mina Kimes assigns blame for the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy controversy
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers’ controversial comments about Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy drew all sorts of reactions online, but they probably shouldn’t have come as the biggest surprise, considering their tenure together with the Green Bay Packers also ended poorly, albeit in a much less public manner. Their reunion lasted 10 games before the Steelers released a shocking statement late Tuesday night announcing Rodgers had been benched and wouldn’t play in this week’s game. Rodgers went scorched earth on Wednesday’s episode of The Pat McAfee Show , accusing McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, alluding to the Steelers’ head coach struggling to keep up with the rigors of coaching an NFL team, and maintaining that the coach held a grudge against him from how things ended in Green Bay. Following Rodgers tell-all, McCarthy danced around the accusations and asserted that he is still the right man to lead the franchise. Reports emerged that suggested that Rodgers gave Pittsburgh an ultimatum over play-calling responsibilities , and the franchise called him on it, resultin in his benching. Rodgers has received the lion’s share of the blame for airing out his dirty laundry in a public manner, but ESPN’s Mina Kimes, at least, thinks that the Steelers should have seen this coming. “The Steelers organization is the one who deserves the most blame. The front office and ownership,” Kimes said. “It was all so god damn predictable. That’s what I’ll say. Everybody was shocked when this reunion happened cause we all knew they didn’t like each other.” Kimes added that “the football was also very predictable,” noting that Rodgers and the Steelers offense were putting up league-worst numbers. “It’s not like the Steelers didn’t know any of this,” she continued. “They made a terrible football decision, but also a terrible people management decision. And they, to me, deserve more blame than anyone in all this. “This was a disaster entirely of their own making. It was kinda the most predictable ending to all this, and nobody should be surprised… It’s like when you have two friends who are exes who get back together, and every single person in the friend group is like, ‘This is a horrible idea,’ but nobody will say it to their faces.” The post Mina Kimes assigns blame for the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy controversy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: AF Corse Expands IMSA GTD Effort For 2027 Season
item.description: A driver navigates the course during the GTP/GTD Pro Practice 1 session for the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship at the Chevrolet Detroit Grand Prix presented by Lear in Detroit on Friday, May 29, 2026. AF Corse is no longer just a guest at the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. In 2027, the Italian team will launch its inaugural full-season GTD campaign. They will field the No. 50 Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO across the entire schedule. This move comes after the team won the 2025 GTD title and secured six WeatherTech Championship wins. The plan includes a second car, the No. 21, reserved for the Rolex 24 At Daytona. Matias Perez Companc and Nicklas Nielsen will drive the full season in the No. 50 entry, according to Sportscar365 . The team made this announcement on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. The shift to a full season shows a major commitment to the American series. It builds on a history of strong endurance racing results. Lilou Wadoux will join for the Michelin Endurance Cup rounds. Arthur Leclerc completes the four-driver roster for the season opener in Florida. This lineup brings together experienced racers and official factory drivers. A New Era for the No. 50 Ferrari The core of this effort is the partnership between Matias Perez Companc and Nicklas Nielsen. Perez Companc has a deep history with the program. He competed in the GT World Challenge America Pro class last season. He and Frederik Schandorff won an overall race at Barber Motorsports Park in September. Nielsen brings his own experience to the seat. He raced in the team’s Hypercar program for the FIA World Endurance Championship over the last two seasons. The car itself is the Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO. This machine sits at the heart of the North American program. According to the team, it stands prepared to tackle the challenges inherent in IMSA competition. They will start with the legendary 24 Hours of Daytona. The full-season GTD program will run in the traditional blue livery of the Perez Companc family. This visual identity has been a staple for the team. The expansion signals that AF Corse plans to stay for the long haul. Star Power for the Rolex 24 The Rolex 24 At Daytona will feature a second entry in GTD Pro. The No. 21 Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO will feature the classic rosso red livery. Four drivers will share the wheel for this one-off effort. Simon Mann leads the group. Since 2021, he has consistently competed in the No. 21 Ferrari. At the March Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring, Mann assisted the team in claiming a GTD victory. His 25th career IMSA start will occur at Daytona. Alec Udell is the lone American among the eight drivers in the two cars. He brings 26 WeatherTech Championship starts, the most of the group. His best finish is a second place at Lime Rock Park in 2023. Tommaso Mosca returns after finishing fifth in the No. 21 entry at the 2026 Rolex 24. item.title: Chargers make QB move as Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Chargers make QB move as Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers are currently gearing up for their upcoming home game vs the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon. The Chargers are coming off an ugly home loss to the New York Jets in a game in which quarterback Justin Herbert went down with a concussion. Now, the team has made an interesting roster move ahead of the Patriots game. “With Justin Herbert in the NFL’s concussion protocol, the #Chargers signed QB Jake Browning to the active roster,’ reported NFL insider Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Browning is an NFL veteran who has started games in the league before, although Los Angeles will certainly hope that Herbert is able to clear the concussion protocol at some point in the next three days before the game against the Patriots. Funnily enough, the game between Los Angeles and New England was initially intended to be a primetime game, but the league stepped in and pulled it out of that slot once it became clear that both the Patriots, who recently lost quarterback Drake Maye for potentially the rest of the season, and the Chargers, who have just one win this year, were not exactly a great showcase for a national audience, instead moving the Cleveland Browns vs Las Vegas Raiders matchup into that spot. At this point, the only thing the Chargers are truly competing for is the number one pick in the draft, so from that perspective, having Herbert miss time might not be the worst thing in the world, even as getting him back to full health remains the number one priority. item.title: 5 things to be thankful for as an Indiana Hoosier in 2026
item.description: Nov 20, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Hoosiers guard Markus Burton (5) celebrates as Indiana Hoosiers head coach Darian DeVries is interviewed after the game against the Kentucky Wildcats at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s November in Indiana. Most of the leaves are off of most of the trees, the squeaks of sneakers on linoleum is ringing through fieldhouses around the state and, this week at least, plates are looking almost as full as Indiana football’s trophy case. There’s a lot to be thankful for as an Indiana Hoosier in 2026. With this in mind, here’s a few things that stick out to us here at The Crimson Quarry: Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android for coverage of the Hoosiers and all your favorite teams! Men’s basketball is off to its best start to a season in years. Indiana sits at 6-0 and No. 23 in the latest AP Top-25 with wins over Syracyse, Arkansas and rival Kentucky. Darian DeVries and Ryan Carr’s offseason roster reload has shown tremendous early promise with the Hoosiers looking like one of the best rebounding teams in the country, just as they were intended to be. Women’s basketball looks strong, is recruiting as well as ever. Indiana’s turnaround was already in motion prior to last year’s rare NCAA miss from Teri Moren’s program. The Hoosiers brought in one of the top-rated recruiting classes in program history in 2026 and have signed another that’s on the way in 2027. This year’s team has all the hallmark hustle and offensive versatility that’s made Moren’s groups such an enjoyable, winning watch in prior years. The program’s future looks bright. This is, at worst, the fourth best season in Indiana football’s history. Indiana sits at 9-2 on the season, with the two regular season losses being the most in three years under Curt Cignetti. It’s a step back from the 2024 and 2025 seasons, but it’s still a historic achievement at a place like Indiana. Winning a national championship raised the bar in Bloomington, perhaps as much as we’ve seen at any program anywhere, but it’s worth having the perspective of what the program was prior to Cignetti’s arrival, which is lost, somehow, in most national discussions on the Hoosiers. Last, but certainly not least, men’s soccer is in the hunt for the ninth star. Todd Yeagley has another great group on his hands and turned some strong development and offseason moves into winning the Big Ten double this season. The Hoosiers are in the Sweet 16 and set for… somehow, a rematch with Washington for a spot in the College Cup. Darn Good Soup is back in Bloomington. The longtime staple, an absolute treat during the winter months, closed its doors years ago largely due to a drop in traffic from the COVID-19 pandemic. It was able to relaunch with help from The Chocolate Moose, being served inside the latter restaurant, and now has its own location on the west side of town. What about you? item.title: What Suns’ Dillon Brooks said about Rockets star Kevin Durant trash talk that got him ejected
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images What Suns’ Dillon Brooks said about Rockets star Kevin Durant trash talk that got him ejected appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Following the Phoenix Suns ’ 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets during NBA Cup play Wednesday night, forward Dillon Brooks addressed his heated exchange with Kevin Durant that resulted in his ejection in the closing seconds of the game. Brooks received his second technical foul with 23.8 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter after exchanging words with Durant, who also received a technical foul. Speaking with reporters after the game, Brooks downplayed the confrontation , attributing the exchange to the competitive nature of both players, as shared by Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic on X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Just competition. It’s just a battle of will. I think he started out well. So he felt like he could say a couple of things to me. It’s just the competitive nature coming out. We both have it.” Brooks received his first technical foul with 4:31 remaining in the fourth quarter following a separate exchange with Rockets guard Fred VanVleet, who also received a technical. The 30-year-old forward finished with 12 points, six rebounds, four assists and one steal while shooting 5-for-13 from the field and 2-for-2 from the free throw line in 31 minutes. He missed all three of his 3-point attempts. Meanwhile, Durant recorded 20 points and 10 rebounds on 7-for-15 shooting, becoming the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 career points . The two forwards were part of the same blockbuster trade during the 2025 offseason that sent Durant to Houston and Brooks to Phoenix . Dillon Brooks addresses Suns’ NBA Cup elimination following Rockets loss Beyond his ejection, Brooks acknowledged the Suns’ struggles with late-game execution. “We played well. We’re seeing in those games that it comes down to the end of making the right play at the right time. I think we’re right there, but we just got to keep it going and be real detailed at the end of the game.” Wednesday’s loss snapped Phoenix’s four-game winning streak and dropped the Suns to 9-8. It also eliminated them from NBA Cup contention after going 1-2 in West Group A with a minus-nine point differential. The Suns will return to action Friday when they host the Dallas Mavericks (11-7) at 6 p.m. PT. item.title: ‘Totally Unfounded’ — NFL Legend Tom Brady Shrugs Off Giants RB Cam Skattebo’s Take on Backflips
item.description: ‘Totally Unfounded’ -- NFL Legend Tom Brady Shrugs Off Giants RB Cam Skattebo’s Take on Backflips New York running back Cam Skattebo unretired his iconic backflip celebration after helping to close out the Giants’ stunning Week 11 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. Just last week, Skattebo revealed that he was retiring the backflip after Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL and suffered a season-ending injury while jumping to celebrate a sack against the New England Patriots. This week, seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady addressed Skattebo’s comments about the backflip celebration energizing his teammates. Tom Brady Dismisses Cam Skattebo’s Celebration Assertion After the win against the Jaguars, Skattebo revealed why he went back to his celebration after promising to get rid of it. “When energy calls for it, it calls for it,” Skattebo said . “My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring my energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. When that happens, it’s second nature and it’s hard to hold back from.” During a Fox Sports “Power Rankings” segment Wednesday, Brady was asked whether Skattebo’s assertion that he got the team fired up with his celebration was correct, and the NFL legend categorically denied that premise. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “No. No. I think that’s totally unfounded. I think what gets everyone fired up is the touchdown. The celebration is, you know, whatever. That’s for the new school, Gen Z. They’re good with that,” Brady said . Skattebo has had a mixed season so far, and the Giants reportedly offered the Indianapolis Colts second- and fifth-round picks for Jonathan Taylor before the trade deadline, but Indianapolis did not accept the package. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer The running back has struggled at times, with five fumbles on 147 touches this season, and Skattebo also finished without a touch against the New Orleans Saints in October, when Najee Harris started at running back, though Harbaugh said afterward that Skattebo had not been benched and that his lack of carries was not by design. Despite his shaky performances at times, Skattebo was trusted to run down the clock during Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, which he did with aplomb. Skattebo’s coach, John Harbaugh, laughed off the running back’s dangerous celebration during his postgame news conference. “He couldn’t help himself, could he? He just couldn’t help himself,” Harbaugh said. Skattebo avoided injury, and the Giants sealed a monumental win against one of the league’s best teams this season, cementing their place atop the NFC East with a 6-3-1 record. The former Arizona State Sun Devils standout has amassed 530 rushing yards and 4 touchdowns on 130 carries for the Giants this season, earning the league’s 37th rank on PFN’s NFL RB Impact metric with a grade of 70.2. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Why isn’t the Las Vegas Raiders defense good enough
item.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stop me if you’ve heard this before, but the Las Vegas Raiders defense has got a lot of growing to do to catch up with the offense. They have come within one score of, or surpassed, the 40-point threshold for the sixth time in 11 games. Pointing fingers Head coach Klint Kubiak said they win as a team and lose as a team; refusing to point fingers is noble and expected of the head coach. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard elected not to take the high road, instead making a snide comment: “Fatigue makes cowards of us all…when you’re on the field a long time, mistakes tend to happen more often.” But here, we aren’t limited by nobility; Leonard would have gotten a pass until he decided to open his mouth and speak on an offense ranking 29 th in time of possession but 6 th in total points. So let us start by looking at who has been truly responsible for this lackluster defense. Leonard is the one calling the defensive plays and maintaining a league-worst defensive efficiency allowed, a paltry 48.1% defensive success rate and a 15.9% explosive play rate. No rush at all No one is doing jack up front for the Raiders defensive line outside of Maxx Crosby. Over the last three weeks, the Raiders defensive line has 2.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, seven quarterback hits, 1 forced fumble and two pass breakups. Crosby is the owner of every single one of those stats except one quarterback hit from Kwity Paye, Malcolm Koonce and Tonka Hemingway, along with the 0.5 sack, forced fumble and two pass breakups that Folorunso Fatukasi has produced. Kwity Paye , a high-priced free agent acquisition, hasn’t had a sack since Week 6 at home against the Buffalo Bills. Coincidentally, that happened to be the date of his last tackle for loss as well. His last quarterback hit was against Brock Purdy in Week 9. Hardly worthy of his lofty three-year, $48 million ($16 million average) contract. Cutting him with a June-1 designation saves roughly $6.01 million, with $16.824 million (one year’s salary) dead cap. At the rate of one sack every 5-6 weeks, one quarterback hit roughly every 2-3 weeks and a tackle for loss every six weeks, the rubber is going to have to meet the road at some point. Malcolm Koonce, last year Koonce got a pass for coming off an injured knee and was kept over a more deserving K’Lavon Chaisson. After receiving a good-faith one-year $11.01 million contract, his good start to the 2026 season has faded into oblivion along with his productivity. Over the last three games, he has two tackles and a quarterback hit. This season, he has accounted for 12 tackles, seven quarterback hits, three sacks, two forced fumbles and 1 tackle for loss. His last 0.5 sack was in Week 5 against the New England Patriots; the quarterback hit against the Denver Broncos on Sunday was his first impact as a rusher in six weeks. item.title: Milan fight back to beat Olympiacos in Europa League
item.description: FILE PHOTO - The UEFA Europa League logo is pictured at the Europa-Park Stadium. (is associated with: «Milan fight back to beat Olympiacos in Europa League») Harry Langer/dpa AC Milan produced a second-half fightback from 2-0 down to beat Olympiacos 4-2 in Piraeus and kick-start their Europa League campaign. After a low-key start at the Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis, Olympiacos broke the deadlock from a corner in the 31st minute. Former Inter defender Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header against the crossbar and the ball bounced back into the net off Mike Maignan’s arm. Milan – who had lost three of their four previous Europa League games – were close to a swift equalizer in the 35th minute. Alphadjo Cisse raced onto a through pass as Olympiacos keeper Stefan Ortega rushed out, and then stabbed the loose ball goalwards only for Pirola to hack it clear as he slid on into a post. Pirola then missed a chance to double Olympiacos’ lead in stoppage time at the end of the first half when he fired over from 10 yards. Olympiacos, who were unbeaten in Europe with three wins, scored again four minutes into the second half. Remo Freuler found Jota Silva at the edge of the penalty area and he fired the ball past Maignan into the top corner. Milan got themselves back into the match through a fine individual goal from Omari Hutchinson in the 56th minute. The on-loan Nottingham Forest winger picked the ball up on the halfway line and burst down the right before cutting inside at the edge of the penalty area and rolling the ball into the far corner. The Rossoneri struck again in the 63rd minute when Hutchinson sent over a floated cross from the right towards the back post where Cisse nodded the ball past Ortega. Substitute Christian Pulisic completed the turnaround with 20 minutes left when he volleyed home a cross from the right after more quick footwork from Hutchinson. Diego Moreira swept home a fourth in added time following a swift counterattack by Pulisic.

item.title: Rayan fires 10-man Bournemouth to Europa League victory at Celta Vigo
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bournemouth manager Marco Rose salutes the fans following the English Premier League soccer match between AFC Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest at Vitality Stadium. (is associated with: «Rayan fires 10-man Bournemouth to Europa League victory at Celta Vigo») Steven Paston/PA Wire/dpa Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo. It was a remarkable 10th victory in a row in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time. The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafode Diakite was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle. Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Alvaro Rodriguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Victory against Viktoria Plzen in December will almost certainly now be enough to earn direct passage to the last 16.

item.title: Ibrahim Osman stars as Brighton bounce back with Conference League win
item.description: Brighton and Hove Albion's Charalampos Kostoulas celebrates scoring his side's third goal during the UEFA Europa Conference League soccer match between Brighton and Hove Albion and CS Universitatea Craiova at the American Express Stadium. (is associated with: «Ibrahim Osman stars as Brighton bounce back with Conference League win») Gareth Fuller/PA Wire/dpa Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals as his side returned to winning ways by cruising to a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League. Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull. Winger Osman finished a flowing move to set Albion on course to avoid a further unexpected defeat before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the lead. Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback at the Amex Stadium when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O’Riley. Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition on a bitterly cold evening in Sussex.

item.title: The Songs of Thanksgiving 2026
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 14: Los Angeles Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages (44) and second baseman Miguel Rojas (72) stand for the national anthem during the first inning in game three of NLDS between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Between the songs of Halloween and the coming twin deluge of the Whamaggedon and Mariah Carey’s “ All I Want for Christmas. ”On this day of Thanksgiving, if you happen to be hanging out in these virtual halls, it’s time of year to enjoy what should be the song of Thanksgiving: Sailors in Your Mouth by The National. Haunting, memorable, nostalgic, and a little gross, if one needed a better list of adjectives for the holiday. On this note, I’d like to share with you a thought that has been bouncing around in my head for years: most ballplayers’ walk-up songs are terrible. And no, this thought is not an old man shakes his fist at cloud moment. While most ballparks have noise that sort of blends into each other (and Dodger Stadium is a prime example), as I have said elsewhere lately, there is a better way. A good walk-up song should be both catchy and fit the player like a glove. Clayton Kershaw’s “ We Are Young ” by Fun is an excellent example. Yes, Kershaw got progressively grumpier over the years, but the fact remained: when you heard the song, you thought of him. Today is not the day we dissect the teams’ 2026 song choices, as we need to save fun thought exercises for the impending and likely lengthy owner lockout. Instead, we address a line of thought that has persisted for multiple seasons without a proper outlet. A few weeks ago, I had a thought exercise with a friend of mine, Jacki Krestel , former writer with our Midwest cousins, South Side Sox, and a general good egg, about what music she would use if she were the White Sox’s closer. She went with “ Joker and the Thief ” by Wolfmother — excellent choice. In my woolgathering, I never envision myself as the Dodgers’ closer. If pressed as to why, I always dreamed I would be someone like Iron Mike Marshall, the patron saint of showing up and outsmarting batters. My response to the exercise was “ Warriors in Valour ” from the Metaphor: ReFantazio OST, assuming Dodgers PA Announcer Todd Leitz could get through the following “Now pitching, Number 56, Michael J. Elizondo, Esquire” in around 19 seconds. Yes, I’ve given it the notion that much thought. The truth is, my personality lends itself to more understated humor and snark rather than boasting. A nonplussed expression is generally my default, as when I look serious, I tend to observe the shenanigans around me and the sense of intimidation is lost. To complete the thought, in my head, if I were a reliever, I’d have a simple innovation. I would have a song for when entering the game and the Dodgers are winning, and a song for when entering the game when the Dodgers

item.title: LIV Collapse Clears Path For Kings Of The Presidents Cup
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images The dust has finally settled on four years of chaos in professional golf. LIV Golf has ceased to exist and filed for bankruptcy, a development that leaves many former players in limbo. This stance marks a definitive end to the era of disruption and sets a high bar for anyone hoping to return to competitive play. Riley’s comments come as the tour looks toward the 2028 season and the introduction of a potential two-tier structure in America. Golf Monthly says that next year the number of cards available for the 2028 PGA Tour through the DP World Tour will likely decrease. Riley stated plainly that “The DPWT doesn’t want to be used as a stepping stone for former LIV players.” The financial and structural fallout is already visible. During the final stage of Q-School, Thomas Pieters and Ben An tried to secure spots for the 2027 DP World Tour season, whereas Sam Horsfield did not pass the second-stage barrier. A one-year ban applies to LIV participants regarding PGA Tour Q-School entry or return to the PGA Tour following their last LIV event. This rule means Q-School this year is not an option for them. It remains unclear if box-office names like Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau will receive an olive branch from the PGA Tour to compete in 2027. While the tour structure shifts, the impact on team events is becoming equally significant. The collapse of LIV returned several top athletes to the International team for the 2028 Presidents Cup. According to Golf Australia Magazine , the end of LIV means Cam Smith, Joaquin Niemann, and Lucas Herbert might qualify once more for the Internationals. Captain Geoff Ogilvy’s home-soil team, set to play at Kingston Heath, may be boosted by Ryan Fox, Dan Hillier, and potentially Jason Day, Min Woo Lee, and Adam Scott. This roster change addresses the lack of stone-cold winners that hurt the International team during their narrow loss at Medinah. Beyond the team dynamics, old rivalries are resurfacing as the shared umbrella of LIV Golf disappears. Brooks Koepka and Bryson DeChambeau, known for their long-standing feud, are seeing tensions rise again. Seoul Economic Daily notes that Koepka spoke critically about DeChambeau during a press conference before the Farmers Insurance Skins Game. Koepka stated his teammate had poor putting performance during the round and ended up with no reward. This comment refers to the Crypto.com Showdown held two years earlier, where Koepka and DeChambeau faced off against Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler. The McIlroy-Scheffler pairing won that match comfortably, taking home cryptocurrency worth $10 million. The 2028 Presidents Cup at Kingston Heath looms as the next major test for the International team. With potential new members and a captain who understands the pressure, the team aims to end the United States’ 11-straight winning streak. item.title: Bruno Génésio makes French football history 👑
item.description: Bruno Génésio makes French football history 👑 Pep, the King. Olympique de Marseille beat Levski Sofia 1-0 on Thursday evening at the Vélodrome on matchday five of the Europa League's league phase. A second consecutive Europa League win, following their victory away at Leverkusen before the international break, for Marseille... and for Bruno Génésio! The former Lyon, Rennes and Lille manager has now claimed his 42nd European victory with a French club across all continental competitions (Champions League, Cup Winners' Cup, Europa League and Conference League). That tally makes him the coach with the most European wins in charge of a French club! Génésio thus overtakes Guy Roux, who had held the record with 41 European victories. Maestro! item.title: No. 4 New Canaan football grabs early lead, defeats Darien for ninth straight Turkey Bowl victory
item.description: New Canaan celebrates a touchdown on a blocked punt return by Dallas George (11) against Darien during the Turkey Bowl football game on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. (Dave Stewart/Hearst Connecticut Media) DARIEN - The New Canaan football team has made Thanksgiving football its playground for the better part of the past decade. It's no different in 2026. New Canaan forced two turnovers which led to touchdowns in the first 3:05 and rolled to its ninth consecutive Turkey Bowl victory 33-13 over Darien Thursday in Darien. The No. 4-ranked Rams (8-2) had already unofficially secured a Class L tournament berth before the game, but the victory secured a home game for the quarterfinals, which are set for Tuesday. Darien (6-4) can still qualify for the Class L playoffs, but would need bonus points to fall its way. New Canaan's defense was in takeaway mode in the first few minutes. On the second play from scrimmage, a hit by Spencer Schaefer forced a fumble and Thomas Tchakarov recovered at the Darien 22-yard line. Three plays later, Jack Crowell scored on a six-yard run for a 7-0 lead. On the Blue Wave's next possession, Dallas George intercepted a High Dunlop pass and set New Canaan up at the Darien four-yard line. George then carried it in for a four-yard touchdown run and an early 14-0 lead. Kicker Neel Arora followed with field goals of 32 and 35 yards, and a blocked punt by Jack Nicolet led to a 13-yard return by George and the Rams had a 27-0 lead at halftime. The Rams retained the Coaches Memorial Trophy, dedicated in honor of former coaches John Maher of Darien (1945–65) and Joe Sikorski of New Canaan (1949-1969). New Canaan has qualified for the CIAC playoffs for 21 consecutive seasons, a run which started in 2005 when Curt Casali was a junior quarterback. Casali spent 11 years as an MLB catcher, retiring in 2024. The Rams have also won 12 of the last 13 contests with Darien, including in the 2023 and 2024 Class L finals. Darien's lone win during that stretch was in the 2021 Class LL semis and the Wave went on to win the championship that year. Overall in the rivalry, New Canaan now has a 62-39-2 lead, with a 22-9-1 advantage on Thanksgiving. item.title: Mason Posa on Minnesota rivalry: ‘I hate looking at them’
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 14: Mason Posa #8 of the Wisconsin Badgers lines up against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium on November 14, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images In college football, with as much change as we’ve seen over the past few years, there have been questions about whether rivalries still mean as much as they do, given that players have constantly changed schools. Just don’t tell that to Wisconsin Badgers star Mason Posa, who clearly didn’t get the memo. Ahead of this weekend’s matchup against the Minnesota Gophers, the sophomore linebacker didn’t mince words when talking about his opponent. “Yeah, no, it means everything to me,” Posa said about winning this weekend. “I’m kind of losing sleep a little bit just thinking about the game. Just, you know, I really want to beat these guys. And this is a team I can’t stand. I hate looking at them. I hate hearing their name. And, you know, it’s going to be a fun game to play. “And they’re a good football team too. They got good players. They’ve had some really good games, some close games. And they could come at us any other way. So we got to be prepared. And, you know, just really excited to play.” Posa has played with his heart on his sleeve all season long, and the Badgers defense has certainly benefited from it. The star linebacker was recently listed as a finalist for the Butkus Award, given to the best linebacker in the country. Wisconsin is looking to snap a two-game losing streak to the Gophers, who have won four of the last five matchups. The Badgers would also reach eight wins for the first time under Luke Fickell, whose job security has been a hot topic over the past month. So, there’s a lot at stake for Wisconsin, and the pressure is on them heading into the key rivalry game.

item.title: 2027 election: Makinde may succumb to Atiku; I wish he’s with us — Bwala
item.description: Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Policy Communications, Daniel Bwala, has expressed hope that Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde would join the ruling All Progressives Congress and support Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, saying he would prefer the governor to align with them rather than former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Bwala warned that Makinde would betray Southern Nigeria if he backed Atiku in the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the presidency should remain in the South for eight years. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Bwala said he believed Makinde could eventually align with Tinubu, but expressed concern over the governor’s reported political dealings with Atiku. “Seyi Makinde, I have a belief in me that at some point he would even join Asiwaju, but let’s assume he doesn’t. The people he’s leading are not stupid. Power needs to remain in the South for eight years,” he said. Bwala said Makinde’s support for Atiku would amount to a betrayal of the South, given the region’s interest in retaining the presidency beyond Tinubu’s first term. “If he is going to succumb to Atiku Abubakar, he’s betraying the people of the South,” he said. Asked why he believed Makinde might support Atiku, the presidential aide claimed the arrangement had already been agreed to in principle, adding that events would confirm his assertion. “It is already agreed in principle and you will see what I am saying,” Bwala said. He also questioned Makinde’s chances if the governor decided to contest the presidency independently, arguing that he would struggle to defeat Tinubu in Oyo State. Bwala warned that such a move could damage Makinde’s political future. “That means his political career will be dead forever. Now, let’s assume he’s going to stand on his own to become president. How can Seyi defeat Asiwaju in Oyo State?” he said. The presidential aide also ruled out the possibility of either Atiku or Peter Obi stepping down for the other ahead of the election, saying both politicians had strong commitments to their supporters. Bwala said Obi’s supporters, particularly members of the Obidient Movement, expected him to contest the presidency, arguing that withdrawing for another candidate would amount to betraying their trust. “Peter Obi is running, if you ask obedient members, they’ll say because they believe Obi himself must be the president of Nigeria. That is his legitimacy. If Peter Obi now stops running and goes to another person, he has betrayed the trust. He has betrayed the covenant,” he said. He added that Obi was unlikely to step down for another candidate. item.title: Ohio State gets more bad news as criticism mounts for Ryan Day
item.description: An Ohio State Buckeyes helmet sits behind the endzone as the team warms up for its game against the Michigan Wolverines during the NCAA football game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Mich. on Nov. 29, 2025. Ohio State won 27-9. It’s been a rough few weeks for the Ohio State Buckeyes and head coach Ryan Day. Ohio State has dropped three of its last four games and fallen out of the College Football Playoff picture, and the pressure on Day has only continued to grow heading into Saturday’s game against the Michigan Wolverines. Now, things have gotten even worse. Five-star edge rusher David “DJ” Jacobs, one of the top recruits in the country, has decommitted from Ohio State on Thanksgiving, just two days before the Buckeyes’ rivalry game and days before the early signing period. Ohio State’s Disappointing Season The Buckeyes entered the season with national championship expectations, but they’ve stumbled to a 7-4 record. Ohio State lost to Texas in Week 2, then fell to USC, Oregon, and Nebraska after star quarterback Julian Sayin suffered a season-ending arm injury. The criticism has been coming from everywhere. Ohio State legend Cris Carter ripped the program this week, questioning the communication within the coaching staff and saying that “the film looks like we ain’t got no heart.” Some Buckeye fans have already laid out the case for firing Day , pointing to the program’s failures in player development and game management. And with Michigan coming to Columbus on Saturday, Day’s seat is only going to get hotter if the Buckeyes lose. Jacobs Decommits On Thursday afternoon, national recruiting reporter Hayes Fawcett broke the news that Jacobs had backed off his commitment from Ohio State. “BREAKING: Five-Star Plus+ EDGE David ‘DJ’ Jacobs has Decommitted from Ohio State, he tells me for @Rivals. He’s ranked as the No. 1 Recruit in the 2027 Class,” Fawcett wrote . Jacobs, a 6-foot-5 edge rusher from Blessed Trinity Catholic in Roswell, Georgia, is the top-ranked edge rusher in the 2027 class and the No. 2 overall prospect in the 247Sports composite. He was the crown jewel of Ohio State’s 2027 class. Jacobs committed to the Buckeyes last December, announcing his decision on live television just days before Ohio State’s College Football Playoff quarterfinal against Miami. He picked Ohio State over a long list of suitors, including Georgia, where his father played, as well as Miami and Texas A&M. Tennessee and Georgia have continued to pursue him throughout his commitment, and both are expected to be in the mix now that his recruitment is back open. Needless to say, losing the top recruit in the country on Thanksgiving is about the last thing Day needed heading into The Game. item.title: 3 storylines for Alabama vs. Auburn in Iron Bowl showdown
item.description: On Saturday night, one of college football's premier annual rivalries will be renewed when Alabama hosts Auburn for the latest chapter of the Iron Bowl. A storied matchup between two in-state foes, the Crimson Tide have faced Auburn countless times before with high stakes attached, with some of the biggest meetings coming during the Nick Saban era. That has carried over to the Kalen DeBoer era, with this latest matchup once again featuring high stakes for the Crimson Tide in particular. Alabama will enter the Iron Bowl ranked No. 6 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings , as well as still in the mix for a trip to the SEC Championship Game. As a result, when it comes to making the playoff, all the Tide have to do is win and they are in. Following are three storylines to watch for Saturday night when Alabama and Auburn collide in the latest Iron Bowl. Will Alabama continue recent Iron Bowl success in Tuscaloosa? Not only has Alabama won the last six games against Auburn dating back to the 2020 season, but the Crimson Tide have also owned the recent series in Tuscaloosa winning the last seven, with each game's margin of victory coming by double digits. The last Auburn team to win in Tuscaloosa was the Tigers' 2010 national title winning squad led by Heisman Trophy winning quarterback Cam Newton. Auburn won that game with a second half comeback, 28-27. Can Alabama's defense contain Byrum Brown? Saturday will mark the third time Alabama's defense has faced Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown in his career, with the former USF transfer having torched the Tide on the ground with 200 rushing yards in two prior games, despite struggling as a passer. Brown is certain to provide challenges for the Tide's defense again Saturday when running the ball, and will likely need to see success on the ground as Auburn's leading rusher has been hurt at times this season by turnovers, throwing eight picks. Can Alabama's pass rush take advantage of Auburn offensive line? Alabama's defensive front will be facing an Auburn offensive line that has struggled to protect the quarterback this season, with the Tigers currently ranking among the worst in FBS with 39 sacks allowed over 11 games. Alabama is tied for the fifth-most sacks in the SEC this season with 31, and have racked up a combined 13 during their current four-game winning streak. item.title: 32 Years Later, Disney's Most Notorious Cash-Grab Sequel Is Better Than You Remember
item.description: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

item.title: Eight Short Game Shots Define Scoring Mastery For Serious Golfers
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images A solid short game turns a bad round into a great one by saving strokes inside 80 yards. Golf Monthly identifies eight key shots every player must master to handle sand, rough, and slopes. These include the chip-and-run, chip-pitch, pitch, bunker shot, hybrid bunt, flop, upslope or downslope play, and a shot from the rough. The chip-and-run is the starting point for any good short game when obstacles are absent. According to reports, the shot allows the ball to start rolling earlier and leaves a large amount of green ahead. This method is the safest and most predictable way to knock the ball near the hole. Players should grip down the shaft and stand closer to the ball with 70% of their weight on the front foot. The Chip-Pitch And Pitch Shots When a player needs more carry than a chip but less speed than a full shot, the chip-pitch becomes the answer. This shot works well when a golfer is around 20 yards off the green and has room for the ball to release upon landing. The setup mirrors the chip-and-run but requires a slightly different feel to get the ball airborne without losing control. A standard pitch shot offers even higher flight and more distance. The motion involves more wrist action than the chip, allowing the player to stop the ball quickly on the green. Davies proposes visualizing wrist cock on a zero to five scale, with five indicating the maximum usage for a flop shot. Bunker And Hybrid Bunt Techniques Bunker play requires a specific technique to escape sand without losing distance or direction. The hybrid bunt can be used when a standard wedge does not work. The flop shot demands the most wrist action and is used to get the ball high and soft over an obstacle. It is the most difficult shot on the list and requires a precise touch to avoid hitting it too far or too short. Players must feel the clubhead slide under the ball while keeping their hands ahead of the clubhead at impact. Dealing With Slopes And Rough Slopes affect play, requiring players to adjust their aim and club selection for upslope or downslope lies. A shot from the rough adds another layer of difficulty as thick grass grabs the clubface and reduces spin. Converting three or four shots down to two elevates a player’s game to the next level. Davies stresses that sharp play from inside 80 yards lets a golfer exploit par 5s and short par 4s. The top five finishers at the Final Stage of PGA Tour Q School will earn membership for 2027.

item.title: Five things we learned from Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League
item.description: Five things we learned from Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League Barcelona secured their fourth victory in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League last night, beating Sabah 4-1 away in Baku. The game was a real eye-opener for Hansi Flick for multiple reasons, including the performances of new summer signings as well as the debut of Alex Campos, among others. This comes just in time for Flick as Barcelona gear up for a gruelling December schedule that is going to test the depth of this squad. Here, we will take a look at five things we learnt from Barcelona’s win over Sabah this midweek. Alex Campos looks like a promising talent Campos’ debut performance was indeed one of the highlights in Barcelona’s win over Sabah as the youngster produced a solid cameo in the last 27 minutes of the game. The teenager looked composed on the ball and offered a lot of technical quality when playing out from the back. His maturity, coupled with his versatility, could make an ideal in-house solution for Barcelona’s defensive problem heading into the December period. Campos can indeed operate as the extra central defensive option at a time when the majority of the defence has either struggled with fitness or has been forced to play elsewhere. Balde deserves more opportunities Alejandro Balde made an impression on his rare start. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) Alejandro Balde made a rare appearance against Sabah in the left-back position, having largely spent the season on the bench. The Spaniard didn’t disappoint either and reminded everyone what he can offer to the table. His marauding runs caused problems for the Sabah defence while adding more width to the Barcelona frontline. It allowed Anthony Gordon to operate more centrally as well. Balde notably mustered a brilliant assist for Karim Adeyemi’s goal, but picked up a knock . However, he has not been completely ruled out for the upcoming Deportivo clash. Adeyemi, Gordon and Gabriel Jesus needed this The real stars of the game were Barcelona’s three offensive signings of the summer in Gabriel Jesus, Gordon and Adeyemi. The trio delivered four goals on the night, barely letting Barcelona feel the absence of their star duo Raphinha and Lamine Yamal. Gordon scored a brace and has been named the Player of the Week while Adeyemi looked dangerous with his runs. Gabriel also grew into the game and improved considerably in the second half. Their collective performance is a good sign for Barcelona heading into the December period. Flick’s squad management was spot on Flick also deserves praise for his brilliant squad management, as the German tactician was spot on with his rotations. He managed the game time of Pedri and Dani Olmo brilliantly through a pact , while giving Alex Campos his debut, a move that paid off well. Hansi Flick’s squad rotation was flawless. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) At the same time, Flick was able to ensure rest for players like Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsi whi

item.title: Former Atletico Madrid star defends Vinicius amid Real Madrid criticism: ‘If he scores 24 goals…’
item.description: Former Atletico Madrid star defends Vinicius amid Real Madrid criticism: ‘If he scores 24 goals…’ Vinicius Jr.’s goal was the biggest takeaway for Real Madrid as they secured a thumping 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League this midweek. The Brazilian scored the final goal of the game for Los Blancos . It was also his first goal for Real Madrid in three months, in what has been an underwhelming start to the season for the Brazilian. Although Vinicius has shown early signs of improvement of late, there is still widespread criticism over his performances and whether or not he deserves a place in the starting eleven. Mario Suarez on Vinicius Jr. While Real Madrid remain determined to help Vinicius Jr. get back to full form , former Atletico Madrid player Mario Suarez has offered his two cents on his situation. Vinicius Jr. has scored only two goals this season. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) A one-time Spanish champion with Atleti, Suarez talked about criticism surrounding Vinicius’ goal output, especially in relation to recent praise for Yan Diomande’s defensive work rate. “Football is what it is. Vinicius plays great games many times and, if he doesn’t score goals, he gets criticised. Now it’s praised that Diomande defends more than him,” he told COPE (h/t Defensa Central ). “If Vinicius scores 24 goals from now until the end of the season and Diomande scores 10, however much he defends, Vinicius will be praised more than Diomande. Football is like that and it’s all been invented,” he added. Suarez effectively means that attacking players are judged mainly on their end product, and the same is the case for Vinicius., who won’t be judged at the end of the season based on how much defensive work he puts in. A crucial month ahead for Vini and Diomande Suarez’s comment comes at a time when both Vinicius and Diomande are currently vying for a starting place in the Real Madrid eleven. Vinicius and Diomande are locked in a battle for the starting eleven. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Although Jose Mourinho was able to start both in the same lineup against PSV Eindhoven, it won’t be the case against other opponents, especially when Los Blancos will require a stronger midfield. Vinicius, therefore, will be hoping to capitalise on the early green shoots and continue the momentum into December, when Mourinho will be forced to make rotations due to a congested schedule. For now, though, Diomande may be slightly ahead in the pecking order, having performed brilliantly since the end of the first international break. The Ivorian, though, hasn’t scored in the last four matches so Mourinho himself will have to make some tough decisions in the coming weeks.

item.title: Dricus du Plessis claims UFC shot down Khamzat Chimaev rematch
item.description: Dricus du Plessis and Khamzat Chimaev fought at UFC 319 | Ed Mulholland, Zuffa LLC Dricus du Plessis has been on the hunt for another fight with Khamzat Chimaev, even if the UFC isn’t interested for now. Chimaev defeated du Plessis at UFC 319 to become middleweight champion, only to subsequently lose the title to Sean Strickland at UFC 328. While Chimaev and Strickland settled their business, du Plessis returned to action at UFC Oklahoma City in July to pick up a five-round decision win over former welterweight champion Kamaru Usman. That performance kept du Plessis in the contender picture, which is currently murky with Strickland’s next title defense still to be announced, and Chimaev teasing a move up to light heavyweight while also keeping Strickland in his sights. Du Plessis told Fight Forecast he wanted a rematch with Chimaev, but has so far been denied. “I’ve asked for Khamzat now,” du Plessis said. “I asked for that fight. We said we want that fight and they said, no, they don’t want to do that right now. I said if that’s the next fight they want to make, I’m definitely keen. I’m definitely keen for that fight again. Believe me, he’s not fighting the same guy that he fought that night.” Du Plessis lost a disappointing decision to Chimaev as he struggled to deal with Chimaev’s wrestling for almost the entirety of their fight. He showed improvements in his wrestling defense against Usman, stopping all seven of his takedown attempts (per UFC Stats ). As much as he wants to avenge the Chimaev loss, du Plessis is always open to fighting Strickland again as well. Du Plessis is currently up 2-0 in their series, having won a razor-close split decision at UFC 297 to become champion and then winning another decision in their rematch at UFC 312. He expects a third fight to go the same way. “Absolutely, for me, like I always say, I want to fight for the belt,” du Plessis said when asked if he’s interested in a Strickland trilogy. “If he has the belt, that’s the guy I’m fighting. If that’s what needs to happen, that’s what I’ll do. “Kryptonite. That’s it, some guys just have another guy’s number and that’s it.” Du Plessis has recently been teasing fight news and though he still can’t make any official announcement, he expects his next opponent to be revealed soon. “I want to fight,” du Plessis said. “I said I’ll be ready to fight in February, but we’ve agreed to a fight. Me and the UFC, we’ve come to an agreement, and the big news will be out soon. I’m really happy to announce finally. The next fight, it’s not signed, but I’ve confirmed.”

Head coach Shane Beamer and South Carolina enter the matchup looking to bounce back after two difficult losses. The Gamecocks fell 34-6 to Arkansas before suffering another 34-6 defeat against Georgia. Now, they will have to regroup quickly for one of the most anticipated games on their schedule. Rain is not expected to be a major concern, and winds should be relatively light. Fans attending the game should have pleasant conditions for most of the afternoon, although bringing a light jacket is still a good idea. Why You Should Watch the Gamecocks The biggest reason to watch South Carolina is the rivalry itself. The Palmetto Bowl is one of the most important games on the Gamecocks’ schedule every season, and beating Clemson would give the program a major boost heading into the offseason. South Carolina also has a chance to respond after two disappointing performances. The offense will need to find a rhythm and create more opportunities, while the defense will face the challenge of slowing down a Clemson team that has won three of its last four games. Another interesting storyline is the recent history of this rivalry. The road team has won each of the last six meetings, giving South Carolina a reason to believe it can make another successful trip to Death Valley. A Rivalry Worth Watching South Carolina has one final opportunity to make a statement before the regular season ends. A win over Clemson would provide momentum, restore some confidence and give Gamecock fans something to celebrate. item.title: Maresca insists his players are full of confidence ahead of Arsenal game
item.description: Maresca insists his players are full of confidence ahead of Arsenal game Manchester City are facing a difficult period after going four Premier League matches without a victory, and their next challenge is a meeting with Arsenal . The pressure is increasing on Enzo Maresca as his team looks to rediscover its winning form ahead of a difficult weekend fixture. City have lost three of their last four league matches, leaving them aware of the challenge awaiting them against the Gunners. Their recent results have raised questions about their ability to get back on track, particularly with such a demanding opponent coming up. Arsenal, meanwhile, have continued to perform strongly and remain the leading side in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta’s team has shown consistency across competitions and will approach the match looking to maintain its impressive run. Manchester City prepare for Arsenal test The Gunners’ recent performances mean they will be regarded as favourites by many ahead of the weekend meeting. They have looked more stable than City in recent weeks and will be keen to take advantage of their opponent’s difficult spell. However, City remain a strong team with the quality to compete against Arsenal. Their recent struggles do not mean they will approach the match without confidence, and they will be determined to respond positively. Maresca understands that the upcoming fixture represents another major challenge for his players. He knows they must improve after their recent results, but he also believes the squad has the confidence to approach the game positively. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Maresca calls for patience after difficult run The manager has acknowledged that the club are unhappy with their recent inability to win matches. Speaking via City Xtra , he explained: “For sure, it’s a big game on Sunday [vs Arsenal], but the players have confidence. “We don’t like this kind of moments in terms of not winning games because we want to win the game, the club wants to win games, the players want to win the game – we all want to win games. But unfortunately this moment is like this, we need to be patient, continue to work, learn, and move on.” Maresca’s comments underline the importance of remaining focused despite the disappointing results . City want to return to winning ways, and the Arsenal fixture offers an opportunity to respond against one of their strongest rivals. item.title: Joshua Kimmich continues to believe 100% in Jamal Musiala’s ability to return to top form
item.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images As an outsider, one cannot evaluate Jamal Musiala’s personal life and can only make ill-advised assumptions. But it is clear that Musiala’s professional career has suffered greatly over the last 19 months. He was diagnosed with terrifying absence seizures in April 2025 before injury added insult to injury, with first a muscular injury and then a fractured fibula keeping him out of action. Even after his fibula healed, repeated muscle injuries have ensured that the 23-year-old has not played five games in a row since his absence seizure diagnosis. How awful it must be to have to learn to cope with such a neurological condition while being consistently robbed of one of the greatest joys of one’s life—playing football. How can someone come back from this? Bayern’s vice captain, Joshua Kimmich, has witnessed most of his journey, though, and is not plagued by any doubts. Asked how confident he is that Musiala will return to his usual level, Bayern’s No. 6 made his thoughts very clear: “100 percent. As I just said, I think the important thing for him now is to get a few games under his belt in succession so that he can find his rhythm again. Of course, there’s a certain amount of pressure on him because expectations are high, and he also expects a lot from himself. You sometimes think you can come back in and immediately decide games,” Kimmich admitte d (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), before explaining why this line of thinking is simply not realistic. “I do n’t think we should expect miracles right now, and that’s not just the case with Jamal but also with all the other injured players who will eventually return. When you’ve been out for such a long time, it naturally takes time to get back into your rhythm. But judging by what I see from him in training, he should continue to cause opponent s plenty of problems.” The most important thing the club and the players can do right now is support the player and give him the time he simply has not had for nearly two years to find his form and fitness again. item.title: Ford’s New GT41 Hypercar Revives Its Le Mans Rivalry With Ferrari
item.description: 2027 Ford GT41 Le Mans Hypercar: What We Know Frank Markus - MotorTrend Ford has declared itself “America’s Racing Team.” Whadabout Haas and Cadillac? Those two each campaign cars in Formula 1. Or the American Racing Team? Well, the former two don’t compete across as many series, and latter only competes on two wheels in Moto2. Ford’s case for claiming the America’s Team title is that it competes on the world stage in loads of series—the FIA World Endurance Championship and IMSA GT3-spec GTD classes, GT World Challenge, DTM, and the Asian Le Mans Series. And in F1, it’s a technical partner in Red Bull-Ford Powertrains. The Blue Oval also runs in the SCORE Baja racing category. And Ford in 2027 will again return to the WEC’s Hypercar ranks—the top class in Le Mans–style sports car racing. Ford Ford’s Le Mans History Even moviegoing casual motorsports followers know Ford campaigned GT40s at Le Mans from 1964 through 1967, vanquishing Enzo Ferrari’s best in 1966 while competing in the series’ top Prototype P +5.0 class, running 427-cubic-inch engines. Then privateers in GT40s took the overall Le Mans wins in 1968 and ’69 campaigning 4.9-liter GT40s in a homologated Group 4 Sports Car class. Ford returned in 2016, entering a twin-turbo V-6-powered GT and winning a similar homologated road car class in the French endurance race, LMGTE Pro. But did you know that a Ford competed in the very first Le Mans race in 1923? French Ford dealer Charles Montier drove a Model T for 97 laps, averaging 43.4 mph, to finish seventh in class and 14th overall. Preproduction vehicle. Not available for purchase. Ford LMDh This Time Around In celebration of the 60th anniversary of its big 1-2-3 Le Mans achievement, Ford will in 2027 once again contend for the overall win in the series’ top Hypercar class, competing directly against Ferrari. Except the historic rivals are designing their Hypercars according to slightly different rules. To contain costs, Ford is running in LMDh (Le Mans Daytona hybrid), which must utilize one of four spec chassis (Ford has chosen ORECA; the others are supplied by Dallara, Ligier, and Multimatic). The hybrid system is also a spec unit, consisting of a Williams Advanced Engineering (WAE) battery pack powering a 50-kW Bosch motor-generator unit integrated into an Xtrac seven-speed sequential gearbox. Ford is fully responsible for the engine design and development and full integration of the entire powertrain, chassis, body, and aerodynamics. Ferrari competes in LMH (Le Mans Hypercar) and is therefore free to develop its own chassis, engine, and hybrid system. An important difference: LMH allows up to 200 kW (268 hp) applied at the front axle—but only at speeds too high to help with corner exits, and the maximum delivered to all four wheels still can’t exceed a maximum allowable total output. item.title: Barcelona boss Flick smashes Pep Guardiola’s Champions League record
item.description: Barcelona boss Flick smashes Pep Guardiola’s Champions League record Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick this week secured for himself a fresh piece of history on the continent. This came courtesy of his side’s victory over Sabah. Barcelona of course marked their return to action in the Champions League yesterday evening, making the trip to Baku to lock horns with the aforementioned Sabah. When all was said and done, the Catalans emerged comfortable victors, by four goals to one. This took Barca’s tally in this season’s Champions League to 18 goals scored, in just five outings. And as alluded to above, it also proved enough to earn for the club’s headmaster an altogether noteworthy piece of European football history. As revealed by statisticians Opta : ‘Barcelona’s Hansi Flick is the coach whose teams have reached 150 goals in the UEFA Champions League the fastest (49 games) – in 16 fewer games than the previous fastest (Pep Guardiola, 65).’ Flick of course also oversaw a spectacular attacking outfit during his time managing in his home country of Germany, whilst on the bench at Bayern Munich. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: VfL Bochum vs. SV Darmstadt 98
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: VfL Bochum vs. SV Darmstadt 98 VfL Bochum will be looking to return to winning ways when they host SV Darmstadt 98 on Friday evening, with both sides eager to collect valuable points in the battle to move away from the bottom half of the 2. Bundesliga table. The hosts enter Matchday 13 sitting 11th with 14 points from their opening 12 fixtures, while Darmstadt occupy 16th place with 12 points, leaving just two points between the sides heading into their meeting at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion. With the visitors having finally ended their difficult run with an important victory last weekend, Florian Kohfeldt’s side will be hoping to carry that momentum into their trip to Bochum. VfL Bochum Uwe Rösler’s side will be keen to put their disappointing 2-0 defeat against FC St. Pauli behind them after conceding early in both halves at the Millerntor last weekend. The result brought an end to Bochum’s three game unbeaten run in all competitions, leaving them with four wins, two draws and six defeats from their opening 12 league matches. Despite their inconsistent start to the campaign, Friday’s fixture presents an opportunity to move further away from the relegation places against a Darmstadt side currently struggling on their travels. Bochum have scored just 11 goals in the league this season, highlighting an area Rösler will want to improve. However, Philipp Hofmann remains an important attacking outlet, with the striker particularly effective against Friday’s opponents. Indeed, Hofmann has scored 10 goals in 14 competitive appearances against Darmstadt, making the visitors one of his most favourable opponents throughout his career. Speaking ahead of the encounter, Rösler acknowledged the threat posed by Darmstadt’s defensive organisation, particularly from set-pieces. The Bochum head coach explained that the visitors have become more compact since switching to a five-man defensive system, while also identifying their centre-backs as significant attacking threats inside both penalty areas. SV Darmstadt 98 Darmstadt travel to Bochum with renewed confidence after recording an important 3-1 victory over Heidenheim last Friday. The Lilies came from behind to secure all three points, with Lars Kehl scoring twice after Aleksandar Vukotić had also found the net. The result ended a difficult run of results and moved Kohfeldt’s side out of the bottom two. However, their away record remains a major concern heading into Friday’s encounter. Darmstadt have yet to collect a single point on the road in the league this season, having lost all five of their away fixtures. Their overall record currently stands at three wins, three draws and six defeats, with 12 goals scored and 22 conceded. Kohfeldt will be hoping that last weekend’s performance provides a platform for improvement, particularly after his side showed greater confidence in possession and attacking intent against Heidenheim. Then you have the Broncos rookie phenom in Jonah Coleman, fresh off one of the best performances, not only for a rookie, but one of the best fantasy outputs overall in 2026. Both are legit dual-threats, run with power, and punish opposing defenders. And both have exceeded expectations in 2026. With the return of Dowdle in Week 6, Warren's workload hasn't been the same. item.description: UTSA Roadrunners KJ Tenner passes off In the first half of UTSA men's basketball hosting Texas State in the Roadrunners' first game since parting ways with head coach Austin Claunch. (Ronald Cortes) UTSA fell into an early hole and never broke out of a shooting slump, allowing Army to surge to a 79-61 win on Thanksgiving morning in the Convocation Center. The Black Knights (3-5) pushed out to a 15-3 lead in less than five minutes, stretching the margin to 33-14 with about eight minutes to play before halftime. The Roadrunners (4-3) shot 3 for 21 (14.3%) from 3-point range for the game, while the Black Knights hit 11 of 23 (47.8%) from beyond the arc. KJ Tenner led UTSA with 11 points, while JJ Kelly and Isaiah Coleman each scored 10. Entering the game as a double-digit favorite, the Roadrunners had a chance to start 5-2 for the first time since the 2010-11 season. item.title: Massara on Juventus’ January plans: ‘If there are opportunities to improve, we’ll take them’
item.description: Massara on Juventus’ January plans: ‘If there are opportunities to improve, we’ll take them’ Frederic Massara has backed Jeff Ekhator to deliver for Juventus, insisting the young striker’s start against Omonia Nicosia tonight is “not an experiment”. With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb , the Bianconeri’s chief football officer was speaking to Sky Sport Italia before tonight’s Europa League clash at the Allianz Stadium. Kick-off is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT] and you can follow all the action, as it happens, on our Live Blog . “Reaching the play-offs is an important objective. I don’t think it can be achieved tonight, but a win is essential for us,” Massara said. “On paper, it might look like an easy game, but we have to be very wary, because Omonia have the quality to cause us problems.” Asked whether Juventus are working on a new striker for January, he backed Ekhator. “Tonight isn’t an experiment. Ekhator is a strong Under-21 player who has already shown his qualities in this league. He was born in 2006, and we know how heavy the Juventus shirt is. We mustn’t put excessive pressure on him, but we’re confident he can give us satisfaction.” Jeff Ekhator has completed his transfer from Genoa (juventus.com) Massara on Juventus’ January transfer plans Ekhator was Juventus’ first signing of the summer. He joined from Genoa for a reported €16m transfer fee, plus bonuses, and signed a contract running until 30 June 2031. Massara refused to rule out a move for another forward, but stressed that any deal would have to fit the club’s financial limits. “As for the transfer market, it’s always very early. We have to see what can be done within the financial parameters we must respect. If there are opportunities to improve, we’ll be ready to take them,” he said. FROSINONE, ITALY – AUGUST 23: Frederic Massara Chief Football Officer of Juventus FC looks on during the Serie A match between Frosinone Calcio and Juventus FC at Stadio Benito Stirpe on August 23, 2026 in Frosinone, Italy. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images) He also defended Luciano Spalletti, who has been dealing with a long injury list that includes Kenan Yildiz, Khéphren Thuram and captain Manuel Locatelli. “First of all, we hope to get some players back. The coach isn’t looking for excuses, but he’s had to deal with a big emergency. He’s been good in the past at finding solutions in difficult moments.” Spalletti had recently suggested his squad lacked height, but Massara disagreed. “We’re not short of centimetres in this team. I think he was referring to physical characteristics. I’d say we’re pretty well armoured.”

item.title: Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures
item.description: President Donald Trump called Thursday for an investigation into a routine revision of economic growth figures as he pushed his groundless claims of interference in the US midterm elections. Trump lashed out at what he called “FAKE” figures a day after the US Commerce Department strongly revised GDP growth in the third quarter up to 4.3 percent from the previous estimate of 3.4 percent. Such updates are commonplace. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error.” Trump followed up in a lengthy second post for the US Thanksgiving holiday in which he also took aim at a series of perceived enemies and critics of his extensive makeover of the White House. “I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late,” wrote Trump. He added that it was a “RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.” Trump’s allegation of deliberate action echoes his other recent baseless claims calling into doubt his Republican Party’s brutal defeat in the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats won control of Congress as voters hammered Trump’s Republicans over economic headwinds sparked by the Iran war and the president’s chaotic tariff policies. Throughout his two presidencies, the 80-year-old Trump has repeatedly attacked the political, legal and economic norms that have long underpinned US democracy. Trump has previously defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom. Issuing its new GDP estimate on Wednesday, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis said the growth “primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports.” Vanguard News The post Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG hails Davido, Asake, others over 2027 Grammy nominations
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Federal Government has congratulated Nigerian music stars Davido, Tems, Asake, Ayra Starr, Wizkid and Burna Boy following their nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, congratulated the artistes in a post on her official X account on Thursday, describing their nominations as a source of pride for the country. Musawa noted that Nigerian artistes accounted for three of the five nominees in the Best Global Music Album category and featured in four of the five entries for Best African Music Performance. “Your music travels because it is yours. Every record also employs producers, engineers, dancers and crews, and protecting what creators own is at the heart of our work,” she wrote. She added that the country would be cheering the Nigerian nominees at the awards ceremony scheduled for February 7, 2027. The Recording Academy announced the nominees on November 16, with the six Nigerian artistes earning recognition across five categories. In the Best African Music Performance category, Asake received a nomination for his song ‘Gratitude’, while his collaboration with Wizkid, ‘Jogodo’, also made the list. Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr earned a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’. Davido, Ayra Starr and Tems also secured nominations in the Best Global Music Album category for their respective projects, ‘Oriadé’, ‘Starrgirl’ and ‘Love Is a Kingdom’. Burna Boy earned a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira. Tems further received nominations in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for her song ‘What You Need’. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States, on February 7, 2027. The post FG hails Davido, Asake, others over 2027 Grammy nominations appeared first on Vanguard News .
