item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and res

item.title: UNICEF, NGE, DAME others make case for 18.3m out-of-school children
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners have called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million out-of-school children in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. “In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. She urged journalists to go beyond reporting statistics and highlight the experiences of vulnerable children and families. “Statistics only matter when they move us to protect the child behind the number. item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, justice for survivors
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a special reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s landmark publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said although the achievement deserved celebration, sexual violence remained a difficult issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” The British envoy stressed the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, noting that their voices were essential to understanding the challenges they faced and improving access to support and justice. He said the UK remained committed to ending violence against women and girls in all its forms through development partnerships, programmes and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. Baxter disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit focusing on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches, tools and solutions. He also commended the Mirabel Centre for its pioneering work, describing it as a Nigerian organisation addressing local challenges and changing lives through its support for survivors. Earlier, Eze-Anaba said the centre’s journey could not be told without acknowledging the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission. She disclosed that the British High Commission provided funding for the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and opportunities to advocate for survivors. According to her, the achievement was not merely about the number of survivors supported but the quality, dignity and respect with which services were delivered. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors to assess its services and identify areas requiring improvement. item.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. He asked promoters of the slogan to “publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature.” “It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he said then. Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, later visited the families of the victims. Obi also spoke to Channels Television on the slogan. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die,'” he said. Obi was also reported to have said that the slogan “simply means, do not rig the election. We want a free and fair election. It never meant campaign and die.” He also defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement, who carry sticks to political gatherings. He said they have never used them to harm anyone. However, Keyamo dismissed the explanation, saying Obi’s camp was the one casting itself as the aggrieved party. “This is a classic case of the villain playing the victim,” he said. item.title: NAF: Tinubu Approves ₦100m, Houses For Families Of Air Crash Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. We could not bring them home to you, and our inability to recover their remains has made this harder still. But hear me, the sky did not take their honour. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our

item.title: 2027: Nwifuru, Umahi, Anyim rally support for Tinubu
item.description: …Umahi targets 1.3m votes, warns against hate speech By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Anyim Pius Anyim; and former Nigerian Ambassador to Greece, Chief Franklin Ogbuewu, have mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. They declared their support on Thursday during the APC’s state campaign flag-off in Afikpo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. Addressing supporters at the event, Nwifuru described the APC as a comprehensive political party with candidates for all elective positions in the state and urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other party candidates. The governor commended Tinubu for what he described as massive infrastructure development in Afikpo and urged residents to reciprocate the President’s efforts through their votes in 2027. “We are campaigning for all our candidates, beginning with the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On January 16, 2027, you will be voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What you will see on the ballot is the symbol of our great party, the broom. That broom represents the unity that has brought us together and sustained the peace we enjoy. “When you thumbprint on the broom, you have voted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On the same day, you will also vote for our senatorial candidate, Professor Anthony Okorie, a distinguished scholar and accomplished academic. “You will equally vote for our own brother, a very calm, resilient, committed and unassuming person, Elumakama Joseph, who is our House of Representatives candidate,” he said. Nwifuru appealed to political leaders and residents of Afikpo to support all APC candidates, arguing that his ability to represent the state effectively would be strengthened by Tinubu’s re-election. “I am not asking you to vote for me alone. I want you to understand that voting for me without voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will not serve our collective interest. “If you vote for me without supporting President Tinubu, I will not have the necessary political leverage to represent you effectively before him,” he said. The governor further urged residents not to take the Federal Government’s projects in the state for granted, claiming that no previous administration since independence had initiated and commissioned infrastructure projects in Ebonyi on the scale of the Tinubu administration. In his remarks, former SGF Anyim urged residents to demonstrate their support for Nwifuru by voting for Tinubu and other APC candidates. He also called on eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the elections. “Everybody should get ready. Collect your PVCs and ensure that you defend your votes. item.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. Reaffirming his administration’s position on negotiations with armed groups, the governor said: “I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals.” The post Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
item.description: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura. Read full article Comments

item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. item.title: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Saturday conduct a mock test of its voter accreditation technology in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise will take place in 406 polling units across the state’s 18 local government areas between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. INEC said the exercise was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify potential technical challenges ahead of the general elections. In a statement, the Deputy Director and Head of Department, Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, said two polling units had been selected from each of the 203 registration areas in the state. The Commission explained that the test would assess how the BVAS performs under different conditions and enable it to address any technical issues identified before the elections. INEC stressed that the exercise was not an election, adding that no voter would cast a ballot for any candidate or political party. It urged residents of the affected polling units, community leaders, political parties, civil society organisations and journalists to cooperate with its officials to ensure a successful exercise. The Commission also cautioned against the spread of rumours and fake news, urging residents to obtain election-related information only through its official communication channels. It said the mock accreditation exercise was part of its early preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of technology and the conduct of credible elections in 2027. The post INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

item.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
item.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

item.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
item.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
item.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

The milestone was brought to life through engaging brand experiences, expert-led masterclass and personalized beauty moments, celebrating the brands’ journey and their continued commitment to helping people look good, feel good and express themselves with confidence. The interactive session gave guests an opportunity to learn, engage and deepen their appreciation of makeup artistry. Guests also enjoyed personalised shade-matching sessions, helping them discover their ideal complexion matches while experiencing MAC’s newly formulated Skin Tint. Guests explored the MAC collection, engaged with the beauty experts, enjoyed the experience and shopped their favourite products, making the occasion as much about discovery as it was about celebration. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
item.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. "We need to understand what is working, where things are falling short and, crucially, what needs to change," said DCMS Secretary Lisa Nandy. The watchdog won't have to wait long for its

item.title: JJ Abrams’ Sci-Fi Thriller Found-Footage Masterpiece Is Being Removed From Paramount Plus
item.description: In some ways, the best found-footage movie ever made is still The Blair Witch Project . This wasn’t because of the film’s actual quality, but because of the effect it had on audiences back in 1999. When it was released, found-footage movies just weren't a well-known thing and the marketing campaign for the movie made it seem as though the events depicted actually happened. Since then, better found-footage movies have been made that have replay value — a quality The Blair Witch Project sorely lacks — but none since have ever tricked audiences quite so effectively.

item.title: Rocket Lab sending Japanese satellite to orbit on Thanksgiving Day launch: Watch it live
item.description: null Rocket Lab will add another satellite to a growing Japanese Earth-observation constellation today (Nov. 26), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket carrying a radar imaging satellite for Tokyo-based Earth-observation company Synspective is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab 's New Zealand launch site today, during a window that opens at 7:00 p.m. ET (0000 GMT and 1:00 p.m. on Nov. 27 in New Zealand). You can watch the mission, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before liftoff. Space.com will carry the company's stream if, as expected, it's made available. Synspective is building a network of "Strix" spacecraft equipped with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which uses radio waves to generate detailed images of Earth's surface in both day and night lighting, as well as through cloud cover. Today's launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th for Synspective to date, and there are a lot more coming. At the end of September, Rocket Lab announced a deal with the company for an additional 20 Electron missions between 2028 and 2031 — the largest commercial launch contract in the rocket's history. That agreement brought Synspective's total number of contracted Electron flights to 47. Synspective aims to eventually establish a constellation capable of imaging locations anywhere on Earth at intervals of just a few hours. The patch for Rocket Lab's "Night Owls Never Sleep" mission. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) If all goes to plan today, the Electron's kick stage will deploy the Strix satellite into low Earth orbit , 569 kilometers (353.6 miles) above our planet. "Night Owl Never Sleeps" will be the 101st mission to date for Rocket Lab. Ninety-two of them have been orbital flights with Electron; the other nine have been missions with HASTE , a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test sensors and other equipment in the hypersonic flight environment.

item.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace , picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. One case that resembles the early days of bitcoin was the war of the currents between high-voltage AC current and low-voltage DC current in the 1880s-1890s. Both featured big personaliti

item.title: Gov Okpebholo Denies Involvement In Attack On NDC Members, Obi’s Supporters
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has denied allegations linking him, the All Progressives Congress (APC), or its supporters to the alleged violent attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during the party’s activities in Benin City, the state capital. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ehor, headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, and Ekpoma in Esan West, the governor described the allegations as unfounded, insisting that neither the state government nor the APC had any reason to disrupt opposition political activities. ﻿ Okpebholo alleged that the incident involved irresponsible elements who were fighting among themselves, dismissing claims of government involvement. He said his priority remained the development of Edo State, stressing that he would not divert his attention to political violence or activities capable of undermining the progress of the state. The governor recalled that he did not engage thugs during his senatorial and governorship campaigns, alleging that a police officer was killed during the governorship election by individuals he claimed were linked to the opposition. He also vowed to sustain his administration’s crackdown on cultism and other criminal activities, insisting that elections should be conducted based on the principle of one man, one vote. Okpebholo urged residents to participate actively in the electoral process, while thanking APC supporters for their turnout at the rally. Earlier, Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa urged the people to vote for APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections, while party chairman Jarrett Tenebe commended the governor’s efforts in tackling kidnapping and cultism, urging continued support for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. Political thugs on Wednesday attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the NDC in Benin City, after the party said it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was expected to address supporters. The Edo State Coordinator of the party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, said the party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport. Videos obtained by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party convoys, including bullet casings seen on the floor of the party’s campaign office. The incident came barely 48 hours after former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy was also attacked during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, in Delta State on Monday. Last week, the Edo State Police Command commenced an investigation into an attack on the NDC secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men alleged to be members of the Edo State Security Network. item.title: 'Significant number of customer records' pwned in Flight Centre Travel Group breach
item.description: Travel giant Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) says "a significant number of customer records" may have been accessed by "unknown persons" following a cyberattack. The Brisbane-headquartered company said the incident affected a third-party accommodation booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and some independent travel agents. Its disclosure [PDF], filed with the Australian Securities Exchange today, added that it was aware that records were accessed, but cannot definitively say how many were exfiltrated. Flight Centre is working with the supplier and incident response specialist Mandiant to establish the scope of the incident. An initial review suggests most accessed records contained only customer names, some with basic travel information. A "very small percentage" may also include birth dates, email addresses, limited passport details, phone numbers, or, in rare cases, health or mobility information. Flight bookings and corporate travel use separate systems and are unaffected, the company said. "FLT values customer privacy and data security," the company said in its disclosure. "The company understands that an incident like this can be unsettling for customers who may be affected, and we apologize for any concern this causes." Investigations remain ongoing, but FLT has already contained the attack, rotated keys and credentials, and increased system monitoring, it said. The company said it would contact affected customers directly. Its brands continue to operate normally, and travelers should proceed with their plans. Customers should independently verify unexpected messages about their bookings before clicking links, opening attachments, or sharing personal information. The attack on FLT follows others that have hit booking systems in the past year, including those on Booking.com and BWH Hotels . More recently, another Australian business, RMS Cloud, which provides booking software to travel and leisure companies, also acknowledged a breach that led to WhatsApp scams in late October. Numerous reports of travelers being targeted with messages that contained their names and booking details hit local news outlets at the time. Customers were sent convincing messages seemingly from the hotels they had booked, and according to Australia's National Anti-Scam Centre, the scams appeared to be financially motivated. Muhammad Yahya Patel, vCISO and cybersecurity advisor for EMEA at Huntress, said attackers targeting booking systems is a "familiar supply chain story" that has a greater impact than simple data theft. Speaking generally about the risks of exposed travel records, Patel said: "Unlike a compromised email address or phone number, a passport can't be changed easily or quickly. For affected customers, the practical risk extends well beyond the immediate breach. "Passport details combined with names, addresses, and travel history create a comprehensive identity profile that enables document fraud, identity theft, and

item.title: 2027: Don’t Vote for Me If You Won’t Vote Tinubu, Nwifuru Tells Ebonyi Residents
item.description: The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has officially flagged off its 2027 governorship and general election campaigns in Afikpo Local Government Area, with Governor Francis Nwifuru declaring that the party’s campaign is an all-encompassing mission aimed at securing victory for all APC flagbearers, beginning with President Bola Tinubu. ﻿ Leading the charge, Governor Nwifuru, accompanied by his deputy, Princess Patricia Obila, arrived in Afikpo to a rousing welcome from party stalwarts, stakeholders, and thousands of enthusiastic supporters ahead of the grand rally. “We are here to campaign for our party, and our party is very comprehensive,” he said while addressing the massive crowd. “We are here to campaign for all our candidates, starting with President Bola Tinubu. On the first day of the election, you will be voting for President Bola Tinubu. “Vote the broom, the symbol of unity. On that same day, vote for Senator Anthony Ani, and for the great people of Afikpo/Edda Federal Constituency, vote for Joseph Ekumankama.” In a striking display of loyalty, the governor urged Ebonyi electorate to prioritise President Tinubu’s re-election above his own second-term bid, warning that an opposition victory at the federal level would stall ongoing critical infrastructure projects in the state. “If anyone will not vote for the President, that person should not vote for me,” Nwifuru stated firmly, stressing that he would not have the moral standing to face the President if Ebonyi failed to deliver. “Voting for me is not as important as voting for the President. If the President does not win, the opposition will not complete the ongoing projects; they won’t continue them; they will abandon them,” he said. Reiterating the state’s commitment to delivering 1.3 million votes for President Tinubu, Nwifuru urged residents to resist political deception, noting that the President had rewarded Ebonyi generously despite the state giving him only 14 percent of its votes in 2023. “I am not disturbed because I know the President means well for us,” he stated. “No President has ever started and finished a major project in Ebonyi, but Tinubu has done it for us.” “He appointed our own son as the Minister of Works, giving us the biggest ministry. This time around, we owe the President. We are indebted to him for the projects in Ebonyi. Take this message home: no other person will love us the way Tinubu loves us. It is payback time.” The governor pointed to the ongoing Calabar–Abuja Superhighway (Coastal Road corridor) passing through the state and the construction of a new cement factory as tangible proof of federal backing. “The road to Afikpo is evidence of what the President has done for us. The President is not just constructing roads; he is the brain behind our new cement factory. “That factory is under construction because of him, and he has provided the funds for us to build it. Building industries will lift a lot of our people out of poverty,” the governor said.

item.title: The One Reason Nintendo and Rockstar Can Make Games Like Ocarina of Time and GTA 6
item.description: Though wildly different in tone and scope, both Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6 and Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time exemplify the craft of making video games at its finest. Each one is redolent with attention to detail. item.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
item.description: null An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud. This celestial scene was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), that was created by the U.S. Department of Energy. The camera is installed on the National Science Foundation's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Why is it incredible? This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy , which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate . The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy. And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

item.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
item.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

item.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
item.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

In case you haven’t bought it yet, I wanted to share some small but welcome deals happening on the physical and digital versions of the game. Costco members can currently grab the cartridge edition for $62.99, down from its regular price of $69.99 (it’s the only retailer currently discounting the physical version). Both Amazon and Costco are also selling the digital version for $54.99, a small $5 discount. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Where to Buy: $59.99 $54.99 at Amazon (Digital) $69.99 $62.99 at Costco (Physical) Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo’s most groundbreaking titles, having served as its first 3D Zelda game when it launched in 1998. Parts of the original game haven’t aged particularly well — namely some dungeon design and the game’s tricky 3D navigation, since there was only one analog stick at the time — which makes it tough for some to enjoy going back to play the N64 version. Thankfully, the Switch 2 remake introduces several fixes, a host of quality-of-life improvements, and, of course, some lovely visuals that make it a graphics powerhouse by today’s standards. If you go the digital route, a recent Switch 2 update lets you gift games to players in your family group. It doesn’t have to be your actual family, either, just up to eight people you designate as part of your group. The digital game will then appear gift-wrapped on their homescreen. item.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
item.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

item.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
item.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation.
